lede: Nacogdoches is about 70 miles south of our Longview shop. That drive makes the most sense for bigger projects like patios, walls, drainage and full landscape installs, and for Christmas lights.
intro: Yard Dog Landscapes is a family-owned landscaping company based in Longview that takes on projects in Nacogdoches and around Nacogdoches County. Miller Maines founded it in 2017, and the work is done by Miller and a crew of four, never a subcontractor. We are fully insured and rated 5.0 on Google across 111 reviews. Text (903) 522-5291 anytime to set up a free walkthrough and a written, itemized estimate.

Nacogdoches is deeper in the Piney Woods than Longview, and the yards show it. The town is hillier, with streets that roll down toward La Nana and Banita creeks, and plenty of lots have a real grade to them. Tall pines and hardwoods shade the older neighborhoods around downtown and the Stephen F. Austin campus, and the soil runs acidic. This is the town of the Azalea Trail and the big azalea garden at SFA, and azaleas, dogwoods and camellias do well here for good reason. St. Augustine carries the lawns in the shade, and Bermuda only holds on the open, sunny lots.

We will be straight about the distance. Nacogdoches is well over an hour from Longview, so the work we usually make the trip for is the bigger kind: patios and walkways, retaining walls on those slopes, drainage, sod and full landscape installs. Christmas lights too, which start at $1,800 for installs more than an hour from Longview. Weekly mowing this far out is not our usual work, but if you have something smaller in mind, text us anyway. We will tell you honestly what we can take on.
landmarks: SFA Gardens and the Ruby M. Mize Azalea Garden

yard_notes.title: Real slopes
yard_notes.text: Nacogdoches is hillier than most of our service area. Sloped yards shed water fast and wash out beds, which is where walls, terraces and drainage earn their keep.

yard_notes.title: Acidic soil, azalea country
yard_notes.text: Pine needles and rain keep the soil on the acidic side. Azaleas, camellias and dogwoods love it, while lawns often need a soil test and lime more than extra fertilizer.

yard_notes.title: Heavy shade on older streets
yard_notes.text: Tall pines and hardwoods shade much of the older town near downtown and campus. St. Augustine is the grass that holds up there, and the deepest shade is better as a bed than a lawn.

yard_notes.title: Azaleas set the pruning calendar
yard_notes.text: Azaleas set next year's flower buds soon after they bloom in spring. Any shaping has to happen right after bloom, or you cut off next year's show.

faq.q: Does Yard Dog really work in Nacogdoches?
faq.a: Yes. Nacogdoches is about 70 miles south of our shop, so we are honest about what makes the trip work. Patios, retaining walls, drainage, sod and full landscape installs are the jobs we usually drive down for, along with Christmas lights. If you need something smaller, text us anyway. We will tell you straight whether we can take it on.

faq.q: How much do Christmas lights cost in Nacogdoches?
faq.a: Christmas light installs more than an hour from Longview start at $1,800, and Nacogdoches falls in that group. We supply the lights, custom-cut professional C9 lines to your roofline, install them, take them down after the season and store them. Send a photo of the house and we will quote it from a mock-up.

faq.q: Do you offer weekly mowing in Nacogdoches?
faq.a: It is not something we usually do this far from Longview, and we would rather say that up front than miss visits. If we install sod or a landscape for you, we will leave written mowing heights and a care schedule so whoever mows it can keep it healthy. If you want to ask about your address, text us any time.

faq.q: Can I see a design before I commit to a big project?
faq.a: Yes. Our Landscape Design Preview can start from photos and rough measurements you send, which suits a property this far from Longview. It is $199 for flower beds, $449 for hardscape and $999 for a full property, and the fee is credited toward the install if you book within 90 days.

service_angles.lawn-maintenance: Weekly mowing is the one service we rarely run this far from Longview, and we would rather say so up front. If you are putting in new sod or a full landscape with us, we will set you up with mowing heights that fit it. For the shaded St. Augustine that covers so many Nacogdoches lawns, that means three and a half to four inches through summer.
service_angles.leaf-removal: Nacogdoches yards under tall pines and oaks get needles and leaves from October into February, and a wet leaf mat over shaded St. Augustine through winter is how lawns come up dead in spring. Recurring cleanups are hard to run from Longview, but a one-time cleanup paired with bed work or pruning can make sense. Leaf removal is quoted after a walkthrough.
service_angles.fertilization: Pine needle duff and acidic rain push Nacogdoches soil low on pH, and fertilizer cannot do its job until that is corrected, so a soil test comes first and lime follows if the numbers call for it. A full seasonal program is hard to run from this distance, but a test and a corrective feeding alongside a sod or landscape install is doable. Feedings start from about $190 per visit.
service_angles.hedge-trimming: In azalea country, the most common hedge mistake is shearing at the wrong time. Azaleas set next year's buds soon after they bloom, so we shape them right after the spring show and leave them alone after that, while hollies and ligustrum get their cut in early summer. Most hedge jobs run $150 to $800, and they are easiest to schedule alongside other work.
service_angles.tree-shrub-care: Older Nacogdoches yards often have dogwoods, azaleas, camellias and crepe myrtles growing under a tall pine canopy. We prune each on its own clock, azaleas and camellias right after bloom and crepe myrtles thinned in February instead of topped, and we clear dead lower limbs and remove small trees and overgrown shrubs so light reaches the beds. This work is quoted after a walkthrough.
service_angles.tree-planting: Under the Nacogdoches pine canopy, a new tree has to fit the light and space it actually has: redbuds and dogwoods work as understory trees at the edge of the pines, while live oaks and Shumard oaks need open ground and room to spread. We plant October through February so roots settle in before summer. Tree planting is quoted after a walkthrough and pairs well with a landscape install.
service_angles.sod-installation: Shade decides the grass in Nacogdoches: under pines and oaks, St. Augustine is the only common lawn grass that holds on, and the deepest shade is better turned into a bed. On open, sunny lots and slopes, Bermuda roots in and holds the soil. Sod is priced by the pallet, and most projects run $1,500 to $4,700, which is the kind of job we make the drive for.
service_angles.landscaping: A full landscape install is exactly the kind of project we make the drive to Nacogdoches for. The soil is acidic and the shade is heavy, so the plant list leans on azaleas, camellias, hollies and ferns, with heat-tough color saved for the sunny spots. Most projects run $900 to $3,600, and a Landscape Design Preview from your photos can get the plan started before we come out.
service_angles.flower-bed-installation: Flower beds in Nacogdoches usually fight shade, slope or both. On a slope, we shape the bed so water soaks in instead of running off, and in heavy shade we plant azaleas, hydrangeas and other acid-loving shrubs instead of sun annuals that stretch and quit. A $199 flower bed Design Preview from photos is an easy way to start from a distance.
service_angles.mulch-installation: Under Nacogdoches pines, beds collect a layer of needles every year, and pine straw is a fine mulch on its own, especially on a slope where it knits together. Where you want a cleaner look, we edge the bed, pull weeds by hand and lay hardwood mulch 1 to 1.5 inches deep, with no fabric underneath. Most bed refreshes run $600 to $2,400.
service_angles.hardscaping: Patios and walkways are one of the main reasons we make the drive to Nacogdoches. On a hilly lot, a patio often needs the ground cut and leveled first, sometimes with a short wall on the low side to hold the fill, and then we build a compacted crushed stone base and pitch the surface away from the house. Most patio projects run $3,100 to $9,100.
service_angles.retaining-walls: Plenty of Nacogdoches yards slope hard toward the street or down toward a creek, and a retaining wall turns that slope into flat, usable ground and stops beds from washing out. We build on a compacted base with gravel and a drain behind every wall, so water never builds pressure against it. Most walls run $3,000 to $19,000 by height and length.
service_angles.drainage: On a sloped Nacogdoches lot, water picks up speed coming downhill and dumps against whatever sits at the bottom, often a slab or a back patio. We slow it and steer it with swales, French drains and downspout reroutes that outlet to daylight or a pop-up emitter. Most drainage projects run $2,000 to $3,750, with full systems running $3,000 to $4,500.
service_angles.christmas-lights: Christmas lights are one of the main jobs we travel down to Nacogdoches for, and installs more than an hour from Longview start at $1,800. We supply the lights, custom-cut C9 lines to your roofline, take them down after the season and store them for next year. Quotes come from a photo mock-up, in warm white or color, for homes and businesses.

lawn-maintenance.q: Will you mow my yard every week in Nacogdoches?
lawn-maintenance.a: Usually not. Weekly mowing does not justify a drive that long the way a project does, and we would rather tell you that than miss visits. If we install sod or a landscape for you, we will leave written mowing heights and a care schedule so whoever mows it keeps it healthy.

leaf-removal.q: Can you do a one-time leaf cleanup in Nacogdoches?
leaf-removal.a: Sometimes. A big one-time cleanup, especially one paired with bed work, mulch or pruning, can be worth the trip. Recurring passes through the whole fall drop are harder to run from Longview. Text us the address and the size of the lot, and we will tell you honestly.

fertilization.q: Why is my Nacogdoches lawn thin even though I fertilize?
fertilization.a: Often it is shade or pH, not food. St. Augustine needs four to five hours of real sun, and acidic soil under pines holds back what fertilizer can do. A soil test tells you whether lime is the fix. If the shade is too deep for any grass, a bed is the better answer.

hedge-trimming.q: When should azaleas be trimmed in Nacogdoches?
hedge-trimming.a: Right after they finish blooming in spring. Azaleas set next year's flower buds over the summer, so any cut after that costs you blooms. A light shaping after bloom keeps them full. Harder cuts on old, leggy azaleas belong in that same window, and they take a season to fill back in.

tree-shrub-care.q: Do you remove trees in Nacogdoches?
tree-shrub-care.a: We remove small trees and overgrown shrubs as part of pruning and cleanup. Big pines and hardwoods, especially near a house, call for a tree service with the right equipment, and we will tell you when that is the case. Our part is the pruning, shaping and cleanup that keeps the rest of the yard healthy.

tree-planting.q: Can you plant trees on a sloped lot?
tree-planting.a: Yes. On a slope, we set the tree so the root flare sits at grade and build a low berm on the downhill side so water soaks into the root ball instead of running past it. A wide mulch ring keeps the soil from washing. We plant in fall and winter so roots are established before summer.

sod-installation.q: Will sod grow under my pine trees?
sod-installation.a: St. Augustine can, if the spot gets four to five hours of real sun. Under a dense canopy with less than that, no grass holds for long, and you will be replacing it. We look at the light before we quote and will tell you straight if a shade bed is the smarter move.

landscaping.q: Is Nacogdoches too far for a landscape project?
landscaping.a: No. Landscape installs are exactly the kind of project we make the drive for. We do a walkthrough, send a written, itemized estimate, and bring the same crew from start to finish. If you want to see the design first, our Design Preview can start from photos you send us.

flower-bed-installation.q: What grows in a shady bed in Nacogdoches?
flower-bed-installation.a: Azaleas, camellias, hydrangeas, hollies and ferns all handle shade and acidic soil. We save sun-loving annuals for spots that get six hours or more. Sun plants in deep shade stretch out and stop blooming, so we match each plant to the light it actually gets.

mulch-installation.q: Should I use pine straw or hardwood mulch in Nacogdoches?
mulch-installation.a: Both work. Pine straw fits the look under pines and holds well on slopes. Hardwood gives a darker, cleaner look and builds the soil as it breaks down. Whichever you pick, we skip landscape fabric under it and keep it pulled back off stems and trunks.

hardscaping.q: Can you build a patio on a sloped yard?
hardscaping.a: Yes. We cut and level the area, and on steeper ground we add a short retaining or seating wall on the low side to hold the base. Then we compact a crushed stone base and pitch the patio so water runs off and away. Most patio projects run $3,100 to $9,100.

retaining-walls.q: How tall a retaining wall can you build?
retaining-walls.a: We build everything from short garden and seating walls to tall structural walls. Walls over about four feet usually need engineered design and geogrid reinforcement, and we will tell you on the walkthrough if your slope calls for a stamped plan. Short garden walls start at a few thousand dollars, and tall structural walls can pass $20,000.

drainage.q: Water runs down my hill into the back of the house. What fixes that?
drainage.a: Usually a swale or French drain across the slope above the house to catch the water, with a run that carries it to a daylighted outlet or pop-up emitter. We look at where the water comes from before we pick the fix. Most projects run $2,000 to $3,750.

christmas-lights.q: Do you hang Christmas lights in Nacogdoches?
christmas-lights.a: Yes. It is one of the main things we travel that far for. Installs more than an hour from Longview start at $1,800. We quote from a photo mock-up, supply the lights, install custom-cut C9 lines, take them down after the season and store them. Book early, since the season fills up.
